proposed_comments.title: Preserve remap priority and reset text state on reload
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve remap priority and reset text state on reload

**Severity:** `high`

Text replacement currently runs before the existing OS-level shortcut remap handler. A typed character that is also part of a configured shortcut can therefore be buffered or consumed before the higher-priority remap gets a chance to handle it. Settings reloads also replace the mapping tables without clearing the buffered process/window identity, so text typed under the old configuration can complete a trigger from the new configuration.

Run the OS-level shortcut handler first and return immediately when it consumes the event; only then evaluate text replacement, including single-key-remap output that represents real target text. After every settings load, clear the text buffer and its process/window identity so matching restarts from an empty state.

confidence.rationale: The live code calls HandleTextReplacementEvent before HandleOSLevelShortcutRemapEvent and LoadSettings does not reset the new buffer fields. The converged fork changes both paths and its exact head rebuilt successfully.

proposed_comments.title: Keep replacement injection and key pairs consistent
proposed_comments.body:
### Keep replacement injection and key pairs consistent

**Severity:** `high`

After a trigger matches, this suppresses the physical key-down but allows its later key-up through, and every SendInput result is ignored. Target applications can receive an unmatched key-up, while a partial backspace/text injection is still reported as a successful replacement. Re-pressing Shift after injection can also leave the modifier logically down when the user released it during the injected sequence.

Track every trigger key whose key-down is suppressed and consume exactly one matching key-up, even if settings are reloaded before release. Make backspace, modifier release, and Unicode text injection return success/failure and stop the sequence at the first failed SendInput call. Clear the buffer on failure and do not synthesize modifier key-downs after replacement; the next physical press can re-engage the modifier safely.

confidence.rationale: The live handler returns 1 only for key-down matches, does not retain a pending key-up set, ignores all SendVirtualInput results, and re-presses released Shift keys. Focused fork tests cover overlapping suppressed key-ups and injection failure.

proposed_comments.title: Handle AltGr and dead-key translation without corrupting the buffer
proposed_comments.body:
### Handle AltGr and dead-key translation without corrupting the buffer

**Severity:** `high`

AltGr is reported as left Ctrl plus right Alt, so the current modifier guard rejects characters that require AltGr even though they are ordinary printable input. `ToUnicodeEx` can also return a negative count for a dead key; treating every non-positive result as no text leaves the matching buffer out of sync with what the target application receives, and locale-dependent `iswprint` is not a reliable Win32 character classification.

Recognize the left-Ctrl/right-Alt pair as AltGr, temporarily release that pair during replacement injection, and handle a negative ToUnicodeEx result as an empty translated sequence that resets matching state. Validate translated UTF-16 with `GetStringTypeW(CT_CTYPE1)` and reject undefined/control characters. Keep the existing unresolved CapsLock/toggle-state thread as the source of truth for toggle-bit handling rather than posting a duplicate comment.

confidence.rationale: The live guard treats every Ctrl or Alt state as a shortcut modifier and the translation path collapses dead-key and no-character results. The fork implements AltGr handling and Win32 character classification; the separate live CapsLock thread remains unresolved.

proposed_comments.title: Bound text sizes and reject prefix-conflicting triggers
proposed_comments.body:
### Bound text sizes and reject prefix-conflicting triggers

**Severity:** `medium`

The engine accepts unbounded trigger and replacement strings, and it rejects only exact duplicate triggers. Because matching runs after every character, a trigger such as `sun` fires before `sunny` can ever be reached; the editor can therefore save configurations with permanently unreachable replacements. Very large persisted strings also create unbounded hook-time buffering and injection work.

Define shared maximum lengths for trigger and replacement text, enforce them in this engine method and the editor controls, and reject a new trigger when either string is a prefix of the other. Use the same prefix rule in editor validation and when re-enabling a disabled mapping, with a localized conflict error. Add focused tests for both length boundaries and both prefix directions.

confidence.rationale: The live AddTextReplacement checks only empty and exact duplicate values, while the hook searches suffixes on every keystroke. The fork adds shared limits, prefix-conflict validation, localized UI feedback, and passing editor tests.

proposed_comments.title: Make text replacement edits transactional
proposed_comments.body:
### Make text replacement edits transactional

**Severity:** `high`

Edit mode deletes the existing mapping and settings entry before this add/save path runs. The return values from deletion and SaveSettings are ignored, so a duplicate, persistence failure, or interop error can discard the original mapping while the dialog merely reports that the new value failed to save. The in-memory settings list can also diverge from the service configuration.

Make deletion report success and abort the edit if it fails. When adding the replacement or saving settings fails, remove any partially added new trigger and restore the original active mapping. Remove the original settings entry only after the new service state is durable, then add the replacement entry once. Reload the list after failed enable/save operations so UI state reflects the service, and add edit-failure tests that prove the original mapping is neither lost nor duplicated.

confidence.rationale: The live save flow deletes first, ignores DeleteTextReplacementMapping and SaveSettings failures, and mutates the settings list before durability is established. The converged fork adds rollback and its exact editor tests pass.

proposed_comments.title: Rebase and confirm the text replacement trigger UX
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The merge conflict spans the branch against current main, and the maintainer's optional trigger-key question is a product behavior decision rather than a defect with one current RIGHT-side line.
proposed_comments.body:
### Rebase and confirm the text replacement trigger UX

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:**
- `src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEngineLibrary/KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp` - `HandleTextReplacementEvent`
- `src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Controls/UnifiedMappingControl.xaml` - text-trigger editor
- `src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Pages/MainPage.xaml.cs` - text replacement save/edit flow

**Problem:** The live branch conflicts with current `main`, and the maintainer thread asks whether short replacements should require an explicit trigger key such as Space. The PR currently replaces immediately when the typed suffix matches, without documenting or configuring that choice.

**Why it matters:** The conflict prevents integration, while immediate matching makes short, common text easy to replace accidentally. Resolving code conflicts without first deciding the trigger behavior can also leave the editor, persisted model, and hook engine implementing different semantics.

**Suggested change:**
1. Rebase the branch onto current `main` and resolve Keyboard Manager conflicts without discarding newer remap behavior or tests.
2. Choose and document one product behavior: immediate replacement, a required delimiter/trigger key, or a per-mapping option.
3. If a trigger key is used, persist the choice, expose it in the editor, and make the hook include that key in matching and backspace accounting.
4. Keep short-trigger validation and help text consistent with the chosen behavior.
5. Refresh the PR validation steps after rebuilding the complete Keyboard Manager module chain.

**Verification:** Configure one normal multi-character trigger and one short trigger. Type both in ordinary prose and around punctuation, confirm replacement occurs only under the chosen trigger policy, and verify the editor round-trips the setting after restart. Re-run the focused engine/editor text-replacement tests and the Keyboard Manager Debug x64 build after the rebase.

confidence.rationale: GitHub reports mergeable_state=dirty on the unchanged live head, and maintainer moooyo explicitly raised accidental short-trigger activation and an optional trigger key in the upstream conversation.

test_instructions: Open PowerToys Settings, enable Keyboard Manager, and add text replacement mappings with a normal trigger and a short trigger.
Verify empty, oversized, duplicate, and prefix-conflicting triggers are rejected, and a failed edit leaves the original mapping intact.
Type triggers using normal text, Shift, AltGr, and after a single-key remap; confirm only visible contiguous text is replaced and modifier keys are not left stuck.
Reload Keyboard Manager settings while a trigger key is held and confirm the target app receives neither a stale replacement nor an unmatched key-up.
